I've had a beard for a few years and I've always kept it fairly trimmed but now after getting back into shape and lifting I'm looking to up my beard game to viking status. I've heard that oils and balms are almost a necessity for growing out a long beard to keep it neat and soft. What are some of the best of them?
I'm looking for beard balm/oil recommendations.

I've used various oils (Etsy) over the years, am currently using Bluebeards Beard Saver: http://bluebeardsoriginal.com/beard-saver.html

It's more a cream, certainly a LOT more preservatives in it as well (who knows what that'll do to the hairs), and is worlds easier to apply than straight oil. I'm not sure if I'm sold on it or not... smells alright (lime), just a light scent. That's a complaint I have with oils, the scent is typically Very heavy and I subscribe to the idea of 'just enough scent for someone to smell when they're right next to you' (vs the 'you can smell them 3 miles away, while you're upwind'). I know some people use oils in a spray bottle to ease with application and in all cases you'll need either a comb or a brush to Thoroughly distribute whatever product you decide upon.

I do weekly conditioning with coconut oil too. I rub in as much as possible (the hairs saturate and instead of soaking in more, it sorta beads on top), let it sit for 30~60 minutes and then shower with just a hot-water rinse. No shampoo ever touches more than the tops of my sideburns. I use Mane and Tail conditioner for "cleaning" in the shower, helps with conditioning too but isn't a one-stop shop in that regard.
Thanks for the response. I've been shampooing my beard as I wash my hair. Is that ill advised?

Generally, shampoo strips out oil from hair. Head hair generates a lot more oil than facial hair, so shampoo tends to be Overly aggressive for beards. There's actually a whole "No Poo" movement : https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_poo

I don't use shampoo on my face (unless I've Really drug my beard through something nasty, maybe if I goof and dump an oil-change on my face), but I'm far from the end all, be all knowledge... Very far, actually closer to the "don't know jack" side of things.

The key to all of this is polycentric governance. Firstly, rules should be developed organically. Rules that come down from above are not necessarily going to be bad but universal rules are by definition going to limit our options. Individual subverses should develop their own rules and those rules should be shaped by the people that make up the subverse. Moderators can either act in accordance to what the people want or, as we've all done, the people should move to new subverses. It's not that rules are bad, it's that communities should adopt rules voluntarily. That was, a long time ago, what made reddit great and it is what makes Voat great.

With that said, subs should develop a system whereby members can have some say over who the mods are. No one system is optimal; a variety should tried and tailored to each individual sub. We should all question subs that don't make accommodations in some capacity.
